provenance: Tool metadata read from the published algenta-mcp 1.0.17 PyPI package (algenta_mcp.registry.TOOLS). The Algenta engine itself is proprietary; this JSON is only the public MCP surface's names and descriptions, vendored so the Space shows the real registry.

selection.description: Legacy compatibility field for chosen table/query/path. Use the selection object returned in choices when resuming a legacy connection flow.

run_id.description: Simulation run_id that produced this decision (from simulate or recommend).

context.description: Business context — what was the situation when this decision was made?

options_considered.description: All option names that were evaluated.

expected_value.description: Expected outcome value at decision time.

rationale.description: Explanation of why this option was chosen.

risk_pol.description: Probability of loss (0–1) at decision time.

request_hash.description: SHA-256 input fingerprint from the simulation.

result_hash.description: SHA-256 output fingerprint from the simulation.

poll_interval_seconds.description: Delay between status checks while the job is still queued or running.

tools.name: query_batch
tools.description: Execute several governed exact queries in one API call. Use this for multi-metric prompts after choosing a dataset with list_data and get_data_summary. Each item reuses the same structured query contract as query_data; defaults may provide shared dataset_id, filter, limit, and order.

defaults.description: Optional shared exact-query fields applied to each item before execution.

conditions.description: Deterministic non-time predicates applied on the metric source. Use exact column when schema is known, or dimension_hint for generic status/type/category filters. These are record predicates, not SQL clauses.

column.description: Exact source column name for this filter.

dimension_hint.description: Semantic label when the exact column is not known yet.

key.description: Stable identifier for this batch item.

request.description: Exact query_data payload for this item after defaults merge.

tools.name: query_data
tools.description: Execute a structured query against connected data sources. Convert the user's question to a structured intent and call this tool — do NOT try to write SQL or parse column names yourself. The engine resolves column meaning from mathematical relationships and statistical structure only. It works on any dataset without configuration. The governed filter shape is a record-predicate contract over normalized rows, not a SQL predicate language, so it also applies to Redis and other non-SQL sources.  Structural roles (use in metric.role): - derived_measure: the main financial/operational aggregate (revenue, spend, value) - base_measure: counts, quantities, discrete amounts - unit_measure: per-unit prices, rates - ratio: percentages, margins, fill rates (0-1 range) - metric: let the engine pick the best numeric column  If clarification_required is true, or if confidence < 0.85, check the candidates list and ask the user to clarify. Never fabricate column names or SQL.

dataset_id.description: Preferred path. dataset_id returned by connect_data or list_data.

sources.description: Data sources to query. Usually omitted when dataset_id is provided.

dataset_id.description: Dataset ID alias for a registered source.

csv.description: Raw CSV text (use source_id/table for registered sources)

records.description: Inline JSON records (use source_id/table for registered sources)

role.description: Structural role of the column to aggregate.

hint.description: Optional weak signal from user's question (e.g. 'revenue', 'quantity'). Used only as tiebreaker.

aggregation.description: How to aggregate the metric column.

group_by.description: Dimension words from the user's question (e.g. ['customer', 'region']). The engine finds the best matching column.

conditions.description: Deterministic non-time predicates applied on the metric source. Use exact column when schema is known, or dimension_hint for generic status/type/category filters. These are record predicates, not SQL clauses.

column.description: Exact source column name for this filter.

dimension_hint.description: Semantic label when the exact column is not known yet.

limit.description: Top-N limit. Use for 'top 5 customers' type questions.

tools.name: query_repository_graph
tools.description: Query one persisted repository snapshot for dependency, dependent, and change-risk graph edges.

tools.name: query_sql_report
tools.description: Execute a constrained read-only SQL rowset query over authorized datasets. Use this only for wide reports that do not fit the governed exact-query surface. SQL must be a single SELECT/WITH statement over the provided dataset aliases.

sources.description: Authorized datasets made available to the SQL report.

alias.description: Optional SQL table alias for this dataset.

sql.description: Single read-only SELECT or WITH statement.

max_rows.description: Optional row cap, up to the API maximum.

tools.name: recommend
tools.description: Compare multiple named actions/options and get a ranked recommendation. Use when you need to choose between two or more alternatives with uncertainty.

tools.name: record_outcome
tools.description: Close the feedback loop: record what actually happened after a decision was made. Sets actual_outcome and computes outcome_delta = actual - expected. Over time this data measures prediction accuracy and reveals systematic biases.

decision_id.description: Decision ID from log_decision or list_decisions.

outcome_notes.description: Optional explanation of what happened and why.

tools.name: refresh_credits
tools.description: Issue a compatibility credit batch for a quota-governed managed runtime.

tools.name: refresh_data
tools.description: Refresh a saved dataset from its original database/API/object-store origin.

dataset_id.description: Dataset ID from connect_data or list_data.

tools.name: register_source
tools.description: Advanced tool. Register a data source and get full schema profiling + join detection. Profiles every column (type, cardinality, fill rate, distribution). Detects formula relationships (A×B≈C) within the source. Detects join keys to every already-registered source automatically. After registration the source is queryable by name via query_data. Safe to call multiple times — re-registration is a no-op if data is unchanged.

source.description: Data source definition. Provide exactly one of: records, csv, json_str, url.

csv.description: Raw CSV text with header row.

json_str.description: Raw JSON array or object text.

connection.description: Connector config for databases, S3, REST APIs. Example: {"type": "sql", "connection_string": "postgresql://...", "query": "SELECT ..."}

description.description: Optional human description of this source.

tools.name: register_trigger
tools.description: Register a real-time trigger that watches a data source for a threshold condition. When the condition is met, the engine auto-runs the simulation template and optionally fires a webhook. Examples: 'alert me when monthly revenue drops below $80k', 'simulate expansion if Downtown revenue exceeds $200k'.

metric_hint.description: Column or metric name to evaluate (for example 'net_sales' or 'revenue').

direction.description: 'above' fires when metric > threshold; 'below' when < threshold; 'change' fires on any significant change.

aggregation.description: Aggregation to apply before comparing to threshold (default: sum).

simulation_template.description: SimulateRequest-compatible payload to run when trigger fires.

webhook_url.description: Optional HTTPS URL to POST results to when the trigger fires.

execution_webhook_url.description: Optional HTTPS URL to POST the DecisionPlan execution payload to when auto_execute is enabled.

auto_execute.description: When true, automatically dispatch the decision plan to execution_webhook_url after the trigger fires.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this trigger monitors.

mode.description: auto = minimal setup; expert = full distribution control

objective.description: Auto-mode objective. For expert mode, use objective_function.

objective_function.description: Expert-mode expression, for example 'revenue - cost'. Required when mode='expert'.

n_simulations.description: Monte Carlo iteration count. Auto mode accepts 100–100,000; expert mode accepts 100–1,000,000.

variables.description: Input variables as triangular distributions (low, most-likely, high)
